correctness.rationale: With N=4 and central shocks, reflection forces a symmetric five-entry stationary row. Two exact stationary balances give A=(1-r)(3+eta)/[16(r+(1-r)eta)] and B=4/(1+eta)[r/(1-r)+(3+5eta)/8-eta A]. Direct substitution verifies normalization and the remaining balance. Strict modes are exactly A>1 and B>1, equivalent to the displayed independent sharp inequalities by sign analysis of the explicit quadratic. Positivity of B-1 at r=Rplus proves the interval is nonempty. For every fixed N>=4, the zero-noise absorbing gambler's-ruin Green matrix has G(k,j)=N min(k,j)(N-max(k,j))/[j(N-j)]. The stationary interior block resolves to rG+O_N(r²+eta), and the exact stationary mean yields the boundary mass limits when eta=o(r). Strict Green monotonicity and O(1) boundary mass give exactly three strict peaks. Separated local maxima need five positions, so N=4 is minimal. Exact-rational standalone replay corroborates the formulas on 32,580 parameter combinations and several N; it does not prove the infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: The motivating numerical study identifies a specific emergent three-mode phenomenon in a macroscopic opinion-shock voter system, naturally calling for structural modal phase boundaries and a minimal population size. The smallest possible population is proved rather than selected arbitrarily, and its complete two-dimensional parameter region is exact. The all-fixed-N rare-shock occupancy profile identifies both the singular mechanism and relative interior counts, going beyond a single finite example. This is a meaningful classification/boundary at a natural minimum, not a textbook deduction, rename, or unaudited small numerical improvement. Its finite-size, fixed-normalization, strict-PMF scope is explicit.
